title: Git Bisect for Your Data
why_read: An inventive application of database branching (via Neon) to enable 'bisecting' historical data changes is a genuinely clever practical technique worth reading.
analysis: This post applies the concept of git bisect, the technique of binary-searching commit history to find when a bug was introduced, to the problem of finding when a data anomaly first appeared in a database. It uses Neon's ability to create instant, cheap database branches at arbitrary points in time to run targeted queries rather than relying on full backups or slow table scans. The author gives concrete performance numbers, like 1.7 seconds per probe and about 13 probes needed for a 24-hour window at one-minute precision. This is a practical, well-reasoned technique that could genuinely change how engineers debug data correctness issues in production systems.
